content:
SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with experience designing and operating Azure environments, building Terraform networking modules and automating deployments. Background in Windows and Linux systems administration, cloud migration, security baselines and network support. Led a 60-server migration to Azure and works in a three-person team operating a large Azure estate.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID, Azure Monitor, Azure Migrate, Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), VMware
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash, Azure DevOps Pipelines
Containers and deployment: Docker, Kubernetes (AKS), Helm, YAML pipelines
Networking and security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, VNet peering, MFA, conditional access
Administration: Active Directory, Microsoft 365

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.
Mar 2025 – Present
- Operate an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions as part of a three-person cloud team.
- Build Terraform modules for landing zone networking, including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall, private DNS, private endpoints and cross-subscription VNet peering.
- Implement Terraform module tests using Terratest in the pipeline and a nightly drift detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML build, test and deployment pipelines targeting App Service or AKS. Deployment frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most apps.
- Operate AKS upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by developers.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed
Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Established backups and security baselines using MFA and conditional access; developed a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist covering these controls and mailbox auditing.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate. Completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Provided second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 – Dec 2013

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Feb 2024 – Feb 2025: Studied Terraform, built a Proxmox home lab and completed a three-month, part-time online cloud bootcamp in December 2024.
Mar 2020 – Aug 2022: Full-time family caregiving; maintained Azure Administrator knowledge and provided unpaid IT help to family and church.

EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College | 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003) | 2025
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) | 2019

LANGUAGES
Dutch: Native | English: Fluent | Twi: Spoken

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from systems administration into cloud infrastructure engineering. The strongest evidence is specific and measurable: operation of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters, Terraform networking modules, 15 automated application pipelines, and a 60-server Azure migration completed without unplanned downtime. The document is professional, concise, and transparent about career breaks. The main content limitation is that it presents strong implementation experience but gives less explicit evidence of systems architecture, technical proposal leadership, stakeholder engagement, and communication—important aspects of this role. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected when cross-referenced against the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly conventional headings, plain text structure, standard date formats, and keyword-rich skills and experience sections. It should parse well and has a strong AI-screening profile for Azure, Terraform, infrastructure engineering, networking, Kubernetes, Linux, virtual machines, security baselines, and technical operations. Matching is weaker for the exact terms "Terragrunt," "mTLS," "SSL/TLS," "systems architecture," "system design," and "stakeholder engagement." Terragrunt, mTLS, and SSL/TLS are not present in the Original Candidate Information, so they must not be added merely for keyword matching. The use of both "Azure AD / Entra ID" is helpful for current and legacy ATS terminology.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering, Azure design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the ad says AWS is preferred but other major clouds are acceptable. The candidate's Terraform Associate certification and landing-zone networking work are particularly relevant. The main candidate-level gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS and SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, and JVM/full-stack background; these are gaps in the candidate material rather than CV-writing defects and should not be presented as items to add. Systems architecture and system design are only partially evidenced through landing-zone design and migration work. Technical leadership is supported by leading the 60-server migration, but stakeholder engagement and bringing external or cross-functional stakeholders along are not clearly documented. The CV also does not explicitly use the role's terms "technical proposals," "observable," "reliable," or "secure," although some supporting operational evidence is present.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the current summary with a version that uses the job's supported terminology and foregrounds the strongest match: "Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Microsoft Azure environments, developing Terraform infrastructure modules, and automating application deployments. Experienced in cloud infrastructure design, landing-zone networking, systems administration, Azure migration, practical security controls, and platform operations across large VM and AKS estates. Led a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration and currently operate an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters as part of a three-person cloud team." Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT, or stakeholder-management claims.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Cloud and infrastructure" to "Cloud infrastructure and systems architecture" only if the candidate is comfortable using that term to describe the documented landing-zone and migration design work. Keep the listed technologies unchanged, and add the supported keyword "Azure Migrate" to that line because it is demonstrated in the 60-server migration. Add "private DNS" and "VNet peering" to the Networking and security line because they are documented in the Havenstad project and are relevant to the job's network-design requirement.

3. Under "Cloud Engineer (contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.," revise the first two bullets to make design and operational ownership more explicit: change the first bullet to "Operate and help shape the design of an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions as part of a three-person cloud team." Change the second bullet to "Design and build Terraform modules for landing-zone networking, including hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall, private DNS, private endpoints and cross-subscription VNet peering." These changes are supported by the Original Candidate Information and align more directly with "cloud environment design and operation" and "network design."

4. Under "Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services," change the migration bullet to explicitly show technical leadership and systems design: "Led the planning and execution of the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; designed the migration approach and completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime." This remains faithful to the candidate's material while strengthening alignment with technical leadership, analytical thinking, and systems design.

5. Under "Cloud Engineer (contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.," retain the quantified deployment outcome but make the operational/platform relevance clearer by changing the application-pipeline bullet to: "Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML build, test and deployment pipelines targeting App Service or AKS, increasing deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications." This is already substantially present, but using "build, test and deployment pipelines" in one phrase improves ATS matching and readability.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT
6. In the Technical Skills section, retain "Kubernetes (AKS)" and add "Helm" only if the CV's existing claim is intended to reflect the documented portfolio work; the Candidate Portfolio explicitly supports Helm. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT, automotive integration, JVM, or full-stack development because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional, well-structured CV with clear progression from systems administration into cloud infrastructure engineering. It uses quantified evidence effectively: approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, 60 migrated servers, nine small-business clients, and measurable deployment-frequency improvement. The current role is appropriately prioritised, and the CV transparently explains both career breaks. The strongest content is the combination of Azure operations, Terraform networking, AKS operations, migration delivery, and automation. The main remaining opportunity is to make the systems-architecture and technical-leadership relevance more explicit without overstating the candidate’s experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional reverse-chronological experience, searchable technical keywords, and no parsing risks such as tables, columns, graphics, or headers containing essential information. It should have a high AI/ATS screening probability for Azure-focused cloud infrastructure roles, approximately 85–90%. The CV contains strong matches for Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes/AKS, Linux, virtual machines, networking, security baselines, Azure DevOps, infrastructure as code, and cloud migration. Exact ad terms that are not supported by the candidate’s material—Terragrunt, mTLS, and SSL/TLS—are correctly not included. The only minor ATS opportunity is to use more direct, supported wording such as “cloud infrastructure design and operation,” “network architecture,” and “system design” in the summary or current-role bullets.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the hands-on Azure infrastructure, cloud operation, Terraform, networking, security, Linux, virtual-machine, reliability, and automation aspects of the role. It also demonstrates ownership and technical leadership through the 60-server migration, the landing-zone networking work, and the migration of 15 applications from manual deployments to pipelines. The three-person cloud team and cross-subscription Azure estate support the company’s engineering-led, collaborative, end-to-end ownership model. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background under the advertisement, although AWS is preferred. The candidate’s material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or a backend/full-stack development background; these are genuine alignment gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The CV also provides evidence of technical leadership and client support, but it does not specifically document formal stakeholder-management activities or technical proposals involving external engineering stakeholders.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS ONLY:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the systems-design relevance more explicit using only the documented Azure networking work. For example, change the opening to: “Cloud and infrastructure engineer with experience in Azure cloud infrastructure design and operation, Terraform-based network architecture, and AKS (Kubernetes) operations.” Retain the existing migration, security, and automation content after this sentence.
2. In the Cloud Engineer role at Havenstad Logistics, change “Build Terraform modules for landing zone networking” to “Design and build Terraform modules for landing-zone network architecture,” followed by the existing details: “hub-spoke VNets, Azure Firewall, private DNS, private endpoints and cross-subscription VNet peering.” This makes the system-design and architecture relevance more visible while remaining fully supported.
3. In the Technical Skills section, place “Terraform” first within the infrastructure-as-code line and label it “Terraform modules” rather than implying Terragrunt experience. For example: “Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform modules, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Bash, Azure DevOps Pipelines.” Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, or SSL/TLS unless the candidate later obtains or documents genuine experience with them.
